text:
Noah (Eng - SF): hi team, planning to relocate SF -> Berlin in late July. currently FT US employee. main asks: will my monthly WFH stipend carry over, do i need to change payroll entity, and does my move trigger any German VAT/corporate nexus for Redwood?
Diego (People Ops): congrats! :tada: high-level: yes, payroll usually moves to DE once you're tax resident there. stipend continuation depends on local policy eligibility and country coverage. what's your target date?
Noah (Eng - SF): target move date 2026-07-21, final day in US pay on 2026-07-15.
Avery (Payroll): we prefer cutovers on first of the month but intra-continental moves can be mid-month if needed. we'll do final US pay, then onboard you to German payroll. note: social security timing matters for contributions.
Noah (Eng - SF): i've been getting $150/mo WFH stipend and bought a monitor with a company expense earlier. will that be an issue?
Diego (People Ops): if the monitor was reimbursed while on US payroll, we keep that. recurring stipend can continue from DE payroll if policy covers DE. single equipment reimbursements after cutover would be subject to German tax rules.
US Tax: flag: watch out for US exit tax forms and potential state withholding if you maintain a CA address. also check timing for tax residency change; you may need to file US returns for the year of move.
EU Legal: corporate nexus note: a single employee working from Germany usually creates an employer presence that requires local payroll registration; that alone isn't corporate VAT on sales, but if the employee signs contracts or invoices locally it increases nexus risk.
Noah (Eng - SF): i won't sign contracts or meet customers there, just product work.
Avery (Payroll): workflow: 1) submit relocation form 2) People Ops opens DE payroll ticket 3) Payroll issues final US pay and German onboarding docs 4) benefits packet for DE sent 5) first DE pay on next DE payroll cycle.
Diego (People Ops): link to relocate form: https://hr.redwood.example/relocate. attach passport, lease or arrival confirmation, and preferred cutover date.
Noah (Eng - SF): submitted now. PeopleOpsBot: "Case #R-5784 created and assigned to Diego. Reminder: international payroll cutover SLA 10 business days"
Avery (Payroll): practical: German payroll needs your Steueridentifikationsnummer once you register. until then we may use provisional tax coding. please upload bank details and German tax ID when available.
Diego (People Ops): stipend proration note: the monthly stipend is pro-rated by days under the paying payroll entity. if cutover is 2026-07-21, July stipend will be split pro-rata.
Noah (Eng - SF): thanks. any relocation shipping coverage?
Diego (People Ops): relocation policy covers a shipping allowance; attach quotes to the case.
EU Legal: we'll review if hiring or office activities change. for now low PE risk since no contracting locally.
US Tax: we'll send a checklist for US filings and CA state tie issues.
PeopleOpsBot: "Reminder: upload German tax ID within 21 days of arrival to avoid payroll fallback."
Noah (Eng - SF): appreciate it, thanks team :heart:
